purpose: Machine-readable contract for representing behavioral evidence in the adaptive neuroticism assessment chatbot.
design_principles: Behavioral evidence is not the same as a neuroticism diagnosis.
The constructs are engineered behavioral representations informed by literature, not official Neuroticism dimensions.
Missing evidence must remain unknown rather than being inferred.
Ambiguous evidence may be represented as uncertain.
Questions are generated dynamically; the schema does not define a fixed question sequence.
The existing neuroticism ML model remains separate from behavioral evidence.

universal_attributes.detected: Whether evidence for the construct is present.
universal_attributes.trigger: What initiated the thought or emotional response.
universal_attributes.context: Situation in which the behavior or experience occurs.
universal_attributes.content: Topic or subject of the thought or experience.
universal_attributes.repetition: Whether the same type of thought or response recurs.
universal_attributes.controllability: Ability to control or stop it.
universal_attributes.recovery: How quickly the person returns toward baseline.
universal_attributes.functional_impact: Whether it interferes with normal functioning.
universal_attributes.repeated_pattern: Whether it appears repeatedly across situations.

repetitive_negative_thinking.description: Broad pattern of repetitive, negatively oriented thinking.

worry.description: Future-oriented negative thinking involving possible negative outcomes and related appraisals.

rumination.description: Repetitive thinking about negative experiences, events, self-related concerns, or their causes and consequences.

emotional_reactivity.description: Emotional response characteristics including sensitivity, intensity, persistence, recovery, and perceived control.

social_evaluation.description: Behavioral evidence related to being judged, criticized, evaluated, accepted, or rejected by others.

stress_vulnerability.description: Difficulty coping or feeling overwhelmed under stressful circumstances.

negative_self_evaluation.description: Self-doubt, self-criticism, perceived failure, and perceived inadequacy.

construct_specific_attributes.negative_content: Whether the thought content is negatively valenced.
construct_specific_attributes.temporal_orientation: Whether the experience primarily concerns the past, present, or future.
construct_specific_attributes.negative_outcome: The feared or experienced negative outcome.
construct_specific_attributes.perceived_likelihood: How likely the person believes the negative outcome is.
construct_specific_attributes.perceived_severity: How severe or costly the person believes the outcome would be.
construct_specific_attributes.perceived_coping: How capable the person believes they would be of coping with the situation.
construct_specific_attributes.self_focus: Degree to which the thinking is focused on the self.
construct_specific_attributes.post_event_thinking: Continued thinking after a social or other significant event.
construct_specific_attributes.sensitivity: How readily an emotional response is triggered.
construct_specific_attributes.criticism_sensitivity: Degree of emotional or cognitive response to criticism.
construct_specific_attributes.avoidance: Whether the person avoids relevant situations.
construct_specific_attributes.perceived_judgment: Perception that others are evaluating or judging the person.
construct_specific_attributes.negative_expectation: Expectation of negative social evaluation or outcome.
construct_specific_attributes.feeling_overwhelmed: Whether demands are experienced as difficult to manage.
construct_specific_attributes.coping_difficulty: Difficulty managing or responding effectively to stress.
construct_specific_attributes.self_doubt: Doubt about one's own ability, performance, or adequacy.
construct_specific_attributes.self_criticism: Negative or harsh evaluation of oneself.
construct_specific_attributes.perceived_failure: Interpretation of an event as personal failure.
construct_specific_attributes.perceived_inadequacy: Belief or feeling of not being good enough or capable enough.

evidence_item_contract.source_turn: Conversation turn from which the evidence was extracted, when available.
evidence_item_contract.confidence: Extractor confidence between 0 and 1, when available.

assessment_state_contract.constructs: Current behavioral evidence for each construct.

conversation.recent_responses: Recent conversation responses used for context.

system_boundaries.evidence_extractor: Identifies behavioral evidence from user responses.
system_boundaries.assessment_state: Maintains known, unknown, and uncertain evidence across turns.
system_boundaries.controller: Selects useful missing behavioral evidence to investigate next.
system_boundaries.rag: Retrieves scientifically relevant knowledge for the controller target.
system_boundaries.llm: Generates one understandable, grounded follow-up question.

adaptive_question_rules: Select a target from missing or uncertain evidence rather than a fixed question number.
Prefer one high-value missing attribute at a time.
Do not ask for information that is already sufficiently known unless clarification is needed.
Do not assume an attribute is false because it was not mentioned.
Do not combine several unrelated targets into one question.
Use retrieved knowledge as grounding rather than as a source of fixed question sequences.
safety_rules: Do not claim a single behavioral pattern proves neuroticism.
Do not treat model probability as a clinical diagnosis.
Do not make unsupported causal claims.
